one_liner: Essentia's C++ audio-analysis library compiled to WebAssembly with a JS/TypeScript API; papers benchmark it against Meyda, results unread.
what_it_does: Exposes about 200 Essentia algorithms (spectral features, MFCC, HPCP, key, YIN/PYIN and Melodia pitch, beat tracking, EBU R128 loudness, TensorFlow input features) to browsers and Node.js through a functional API: `new Essentia(EssentiaWASM)` then `essentia.MFCC(spectrumVector)`, returning plain objects of embind VectorFloat handles. Inputs must be converted with `arrayToVector()` and outputs back with `vectorToArray()`. Add-on modules wrap TensorFlow.js models, configurable feature extractors and Plotly plots. It is not a drop-in for Meyda: different API, different algorithm defaults (MFCC uses 40 mel bands, Meyda 26).
how_it_is_fast: Speed comes only from running Essentia's C++ (Emscripten 1.39.19, KISS FFT backend, Eigen) as WebAssembly instead of interpreting pure-JS DSP. The build is not tuned for speed: Makefile.essentiajs compiles with -Oz (size), keeps ASSERTIONS=2 and EXCEPTION_DEBUG in the web build, and uses no wasm SIMD or threads. The generated wrapper (src/cpp/includes/essentiajs.cpp) creates, configures and deletes a new algorithm instance through AlgorithmFactory on every call, so per-frame use pays for filterbank, window and FFT setup each frame; issue #65 reports the unmerged class-based (configure-once) interface gave a 'significant' MFCC speedup, without numbers.
when_to_use: You need MIR algorithms that pure-JS libraries lack (key and chord detection, Melodia/PYIN pitch, beat trackers, EBU R128, NNLS chroma) in a browser, Web Worker, AudioWorklet or Node.js.
You want the same algorithms and defaults as a native or Python Essentia pipeline, so web results match server-side features.
Offline whole-file analysis where a few heavy calls (RhythmExtractor2013, KeyExtractor, TensorflowInputMusiCNN) dominate and the per-call setup cost is amortised.
Feeding the bundled Essentia TensorFlow.js models (MusiCNN, VGGish auto-tagging, mood, genre) from the same feature code used to train them.
AGPL-3.0 is acceptable for your web app, or you can buy a commercial Essentia licence from UPF.
when_not_to_use: Closed-source or SaaS products that cannot meet AGPL-3.0 (network use counts as distribution).

Per-frame calls of cheap features (energy, RMS, ZCR, centroid) in a tight loop: every call re-creates the C++ algorithm and copies data across the JS/wasm boundary, while Meyda caches its mel filterbank between calls; a pure-JS library may be competitive there, and no published number settles it.
Code that cannot manage memory by hand: every VectorFloat returned must be `.delete()`d or the wasm heap grows.

Projects needing a maintained npm package: the last npm release is 0.1.3 (2021-06-24), master's last commit is 2022-07-19 and only a dev branch moved (2024-06-12); the README still says APIs are unstable.
Bundle-size-sensitive pages: the sync UMD/ES builds embed the whole wasm binary as base64 (SINGLE_FILE=1).

integration.dependencies: npm essentia.js (wasm backend plus JS/TS API; node-wav for Node file loading); optional @tensorflow/tfjs for the model add-on and Plotly for plots. Rebuilding needs the Dockerfile's Emscripten 1.39.19 image with Essentia built statically (--fft=KISS) and Eigen 3.3.7.
integration.min_toolchain: Any browser with WebAssembly (Web Audio API for decoding); Node.js (build scripts use Node 12.18.1); TypeScript 3.9 for the typings.
integration.platforms: Browsers (the papers test two desktop browsers plus Android and iOS devices; the benchmark page names Chrome and Firefox), Node.js, Web Workers and AudioWorklet; wasm32 only, no SIMD or threaded build.
integration.thread_safety: not documented; single-threaded wasm module, one instance per worker

gotchas: Benchmark harness flaw (MTG/essentia.js-benchmarks, browser suite src/js/Benchmarks/offline/*.js): the default 'essentia' frame mode calls FrameGenerator, which drops frames that isSilent() flags (essentiajs.cpp line 91) and uses FrameCutter's own framing, while the Meyda side processes every hop of audioBuffer.length/HOP_SIZE frames, so the two sides do not process the same frames; per-algorithm defaults also differ (Essentia MFCC 40 mel bands vs Meyda 26), so timings are not like for like.

The Node runner (node/benchmark/*.js) feeds both libraries the raw WAV file bytes from fs.readFile (header included, never decoded), and index.js forks all suites at once so they contend for CPU. The repo commits no results and pins essentia.js 0.0.9, so it cannot reproduce the papers' figures.

The native-Essentia baseline (python/essentia_algorithms.py) configures each algorithm once outside the frame loop, while Essentia.js re-creates it per frame. Any wasm-vs-native gap reported from this harness therefore mixes wasm overhead with per-call setup cost.

Open correctness bugs: VectorFloat params mis-converted from TypeScript (#136), float params accept numeric strings (#137), FrequencyBands throws uncaught (#108), PitchMelodia returns zeros on microphone input (#149), wrong key output reported (#143).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over tinyfft when you need complete MIR features (MFCC, key, beats, pitch) rather than a raw FFT. Pick it over the TensorFlow.js WASM backend when you need Essentia's audio preprocessing to feed models trained on Essentia features; it uses tfjs for the models themselves.
verified_claims_summary: No measured result could be read: the ISMIR 2020 and TISMIR 2021 papers time Essentia.js against Meyda and native Essentia on two browsers, Node.js and four devices (Android, iOS), but every copy was blocked here, and the benchmark repo commits no results. Whether Essentia.js beats Meyda, and by how much, is unverified; the browser harness behind the papers has a frame-count asymmetry and mismatched algorithm parameters.
status_note: Stale rather than dead: npm 0.1.3 (2021-06), master last commit 2022-07-19, a dev branch active until 2024-06-12 toward a 1.0 roadmap and new issues still filed in 2026; AGPL-3.0, usable from npm without building, but an evidence tier of D: the catalogue entry rests on unread papers and a flawed harness.
